vulnerabilities.description: An issue was found in Python's incremental HTML parser (html.parser.HTMLParser). When application code repeatedly feeds small pieces of attacker-controlled data into the parser while an HTML construct remains unterminated, the parser can be driven to consume disproportionate CPU time, resulting in a denial of service.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to the latest Liquibase Secure release when available. The fix is present in this codebase's own build of the bundled Python runtime, but only a published release carries it to a running deployment.

ratings.justification: None of the check scripts Liquibase bundles and runs by default import html.parser. Reaching the vulnerable code requires a customer to author and configure their own custom check script that does so.

analysis.detail: Liquibase Secure bundles a GraalPy-based embedded Python runtime so that customers can author custom policy-check scripts with full access to the Python standard library, including html.parser. None of the check scripts Liquibase ships and runs by default import html.parser — they parse changeset SQL with a different library. Triggering this issue requires a customer to deliberately author and configure their own custom check script that imports html.parser and feeds it attacker-controlled data; Liquibase creates no such exposure on its own, and no shipped check performs this action.

vulnerabilities.description: An issue was found in Python's tarfile module. TarFile.extract() does not fully apply the filter argument when extracting hardlink members, so a crafted tar archive can cause an extracted file to be written with unexpected ownership even when a restrictive filter such as filter="data" is requested.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to the latest Liquibase Secure release when available. The fix is present in this codebase's own build of the bundled Python runtime, but only a published release carries it to a running deployment.

ratings.justification: None of the check scripts Liquibase bundles and runs by default import tarfile or extract archives. Reaching the vulnerable code requires a customer to author and configure their own custom check script that does so.

analysis.detail: Liquibase Secure bundles a GraalPy-based embedded Python runtime so that customers can author custom policy-check scripts with full access to the Python standard library, including tarfile. None of the check scripts Liquibase ships and runs by default import tarfile — they parse changeset SQL with a different library and never extract archives. Triggering this issue requires a customer to deliberately author and configure their own custom check script that imports tarfile and extracts an untrusted archive; Liquibase creates no such exposure on its own, and no shipped check performs this action.

vulnerabilities.description: The html.parser.HTMLParser class had worst-case quadratic complexity when processing certain crafted malformed inputs at end-of-file, potentially leading to an amplified denial of service.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to the latest Liquibase Secure release when available. The fix is present in this codebase's own build of the bundled Python runtime, but only a published release carries it to a running deployment.
